§4: the operating point is set by discharges, and the golden rows ran 10–65 V above the optimum

Interior efficiency, discharge and burst losses vs HV, pass 1 (det2/3/6/7)

  • Gain doubles every 16.6–19.1 V; discharges rise ×10 every 21–42 V (∝ gain² to gain^2.7).
  • Scan optima 480 / 470 / 480 / 430 V (det2/3/6/7). At the golden 495 V det6/det7 read 74.4 / 68.0 %: discharges take 16.8 / 24.7 %.
  • The > 50-strip veto also removes bursts with no discharge (6.3 % of g_det4, 7–10 % of det6 at low HV).

Decide / open: G quote det6/det7 at the golden HV, at the optima, or both; which chambers “480/480/440 V” names. H bursts: separate class or one spark class.

Source: rerun/paper1_ops/README.md (OPS), rerun/effbudget (EFF), rerun/paper1_charge (CHG)

4

Details

Text → pass 1. “480/480/440 V” = the optima det3 (or det2) / det6 / det7: OK as optima. The golden rows ran at 490 (det3) and 495 V (others). Gain slopes (CHG): ×2 every 16.6 (det2), 16.7 (det3), 19.1 (det6), 17.9 V (det7), curved; an M3-free hits proxy reproduces them and shows the 6-23 night flat for det3 too.

Not re-derived: “Poisson”, “muon-induced 4–6×”, “edge-concentrated” sparks (needs discharge positions and random triggers).

det4: no bench gain curve (6-23: chambers not yet at working gain, CONS §1). At SPS its charge rises only ×1.65 over 580–780 V (run66, CF₄, telescope denominator) and is flat over 550–625 V in Ar/CO₂/iso. Whether its SPS HV path has a series resistor or filter is a question for Stephan.

§4: a discharge costs at most a few ms, and the gain does not sag after it

Efficiency and charge vs time since the previous discharge, all five chambers

  • Dead time per discharge, 95 % UL: ≤ 1–3 ms on the bench chambers.
  • At the golden HV: 0.13–0.17 discharges/s (det2/det3), 0.69 (det6), 1.14 (det7).
  • Confirms the abstract’s “no dead time after a spark”, now measured on all five.

Decide / open: the text’s Poisson / muon-induced / edge claims cannot be re-derived from bench data (no discharge positions, no random triggers): keep, soften, or drop?

Source: rerun/paper1_ops/README.md; discharge = vetoed trigger with a chip ≥ 8 strips over 3000 ADC

§5: the 30 mm fiducial is physical: a drift-field fringe reaches 20–30 mm in from the x sides

det3: turn-on, the other view’s tan bias against M3, the column duration vs distance to the edge

  • Tan bias 0.1–0.36 within 5–20 mm of an x side, ≤ 0.016 beyond 30 mm; its sign flips side to side (drift lines converge inward).
  • Edge strips collect from beyond the strip area: longer columns, more charge.
  • Not the bow: it predicts the opposite sign of edge T.

Decide / open: Q show det3 (the paper’s chamber) or det2 (10× the triggers). det2’s edge-T tension is closed: the two estimators average different bands of a non-monotonic T(d) (predicted −78.5 vs −86 ± 33 ns).

Source: rerun/paper1_figs/README.md (FIGS), rerun/consistency/README.md

8

Details

Replaces the hits-angle edge study (D4, “−3° edge tilt”). Column duration edge − interior: −4 / +26 / +78 / +27 / −115 ns (det2/3/4/6/7); the S4 stack gave −86 / +40 / +60 (det2/3/4). det2 closed (paper1_spsfigs det2_edge_check): T ≈ 584 ns in the outer 0–5 mm, 915–950 at 5–15 mm, 800–860 further in; S4’s sample is 40 % in the outer 5 mm.

Efficiency reaches its plateau ~5 mm in from the y sides and 10–20 mm from the x sides; the 0–5 mm strip on every side loses the column off the strips. A 10–30 mm y band keeps full efficiency, but its Y-angle s68 is 1.3–1.9× worse.

10

Details

Without O₂ at the same water each stack fits 1.5–117× worse (median 33). Closure test passes. Agrees with the pre-pass run71 fit (1.51 % / 163 ppm) once the 30 mm gap and the saturated-event treatment are accounted for.

Degeneracies: water ↔ gap (1.2 mm ≈ 0.12–0.18 % water; O₂ unaffected); gap ↔ pulse shape (the shaper hits its bound at 26.2–27.9 mm, so the gap error is one profile step, 0.9 mm); O₂ ↔ slow electronics droop on ZS stacks (largest O₂ systematic, 81 ppm).

The grid had to grow twice: water edges (CF₄ 1.7 %, CO₂ 2.2 %), field (CO₂ rows to 139 V/cm), O₂ (272 ppm). Midpoint checks: ≤ 0.011 % water, ≤ 16 ppm O₂.

11

Details

Estimator: a step of the row’s own template fitted to the rising edge of the strip-sum waveform up to the first sample above 25 % of its maximum, plus 10 ns × ftst per view. It beats the box fit (85 ns), constant-fraction 30 % (77 ns) and 10 % (49 ns), and is the only one flat in angle (≤ 8 ns to |tan| 0.5).

HV: det3 83 → 21 ns per view (425 → 500 V); drift field: det3 114 → 38.5 ns (104 → 382 V/cm). Trigger test: cov(start, end) −63 ± 19 ns² on sat_det3 (a 39 ns trigger term would give +1500).

Reconciled: the hits 33 ns is the X−Y plane-to-plane number; its waveform equivalent is 22 ns per view; the hits “absolute” 37.7 ns ↔ waveform event time 42 ns.

§8: the ~0.6° angle remainder is per-event charge fluctuation the toy under-generates

X view, calibration rows: measured s68, the toy’s modelled terms, and what is left (FD convention)

measured s68

all toy terms

unexplained U

U on clean events

  • Ruled out: the M3 reference, a cause common to X and Y, sub-tilt-map structure, angle non-linearity, the X copy (Y has it too).
  • Present head-on, flat in angle, fit-visible.
  • K1 is not it: ~0 % of it.

Residual bootstrap: the data’s own fit residuals, added to the toy, carry 105 ± 17 % (det2), 59 ± 10 % (det3) and 54 ± 11 % (det4) of the clean remainder². No named structure (common mode, template, time shape, ±1 asymmetry) is data-specific: the toy under-generates event-to-event charge-pattern fluctuations.

Decide / open: O wording: the 10-27 “not a waveform misfit” is reversed on pass 1, and K1 is ruled out.

Source: rerun/paper1_floor/results/floor_budget.json (FLOOR), K1_TEST_2026-11-01.md; toy re-run on the pass-1 bundles

13

Details

Unexplained part (FD, toy on the pass-1 bundles, 1500 events/angle): det2 0.72 of 0.98°, det3 0.68 of 0.93°, det4 1.52 of 1.62°, det6 0.93 of 1.13°, det7 0.98 of 1.12°: 54–88 % of the X variance. All toy terms 0.38–0.46°; toy floor 0.31–0.34°.

Event conditions the toy doesn’t generate (saturated, bright tail, topology) are 12–37 % of U² (det7 65–92 %). Remainder on clean events 0.56–0.65° (det2/3/7 X), det4 1.42°.

K1-aware weights (toy only): 0.04–0.06° worse on det2/det3 X, so the locked model leaves ≤ 0° there.

Bootstrap (rerun/paper1_floor/BOOTSTRAP_2026-11-01.md): data residuals moved onto toy events move the angle 1.5–2.0× more than the toy’s own (det2/3/4 X 0.243/0.241/0.416° vs 0.123/0.162/0.283°); calibrated by the method’s efficiency ε = 0.29–0.37. What carries the angle in both data and toy residuals: the part coherent in time and across strips (~80 %), antisymmetric about the track (~40 %). Untested candidates (simulation only): Polya θ, δ-ray rate/range, cluster-size distribution, per-event resistive spread. Y view and det7 rest on the data-truth arm only.

§8: in the beam det4 Y resolves 190 µm (176 on run 53); X has no measurement

Chamber term near normal incidence: bench (M3 χ² → 0, minus pointing) and det4 Y at SPS (telescope 3-zone fit)

X: the 3-zone fits fail (χ²/1 7–88; dead stripes in the beam spot), so “X 209 µm” is a model-dependent intercept, not a resolution. Quote Y only.

Decide / open: A run63 Y 190 ± 10 (p0) or run53 Y 176 ± 10 (hits). B now a Y-only choice of estimator. P bench chamber term or the decomposition. “176 µm = 0.30 × pitch” is wrong: 0.23 × pitch.

Source: rerun/paper1_floor/results/position_ms.json (FLOOR), rerun/sps_audit + sps_junk/results/final_rule.json

14

Details

The bench residual (430–620 µm core σ) grows with the M3 χ² of the matching coordinate (det3 Y 298 → 733 µm across quintiles): M3 scattering between its doublets, 240–370 µm. Extrapolated to χ² → 0 minus the pointing P 0.21–0.28 mm: chamber 230–310 µm at all angles; near normal det2 163/176 ± 25, det3 126/116 ± 35 µm. ±10 % on P moves it ~±50 µm.

SPS (final rule): run63 flat700 Y 190 ± 10 (p0, zone fit χ²/1 0.3); run53 Y 176 ± 10 (hits), 155 ± 7 (centroid). X: the zone fits fail (χ²/1 7–88), so the 209 ± 11 (p_mid) is a model-dependent intercept (rerun/paper1_spsfigs/README.md). The telescope term (f 0.25–0.34) is a ±40 µm systematic. Head-on, the fit p0 is noisy in X (angle noise leaks into the mesh position): run63 X 358 µm with p0 vs 294 µm centroid.

The 6-23/6-24 trigger term makes det4’s bench position unquotable: use SPS only.

§6: drying, +13 % step

(a) measured: at a fixed 495 V det3’s charge rose ×4 and det4’s ×7 through the night; efficiency 0.06 → 35 % / 3.9 → 28.5 %. That hides 20–35 % of the gain slope. Likely gas contamination from the chamber changes (inferred).

(b) measured, cause unknown: cov(start, end) +3900–4400 ns² on both chambers vs ≤ +518 on every other night; persists on 6-24 after the gain recovered.

Consequence: det4 bench timing and position are not quotable (SPS only); det4 angles are fine (a common time shift moves position, not slope); the 6-23 water needs a caveat.

Decide / open: facts needed: what changed in the trigger/paddles on 6-23/6-24? Was det3 or det4 opened on 6-22/6-23, and the gas line order?

What this does not rule out

  • The ~0.6° angle remainder (det4 1.4°) is per-event charge fluctuation the toy under-generates; which microphysics (Polya, δ-rays, cluster sizes, resistive spread) is untested.
